Subject: URGENT: TideBank dedicated pool saturation - initial data

Team —

TideBank (TB-4821) reported a production regression: dedicated pool serving their reserved throughput saturated around 07:35–08:05 PT, producing ~3–5% 502s and p95 latency jump to 1.2s. Customer has a live promotion; this is high severity and they want ETA now.

What I have so far:
- Customer-provided logs attached, plus our infra traces show persistent queue depth on pool rdp-03 (node group).
- There’s a spike in large-batch requests from a single tenant (same customer) but with higher-than-expected sequence lengths; KV cache churn appears elevated.
- TideBank is on reserved capacity (no autoscaling beyond defined headroom).

Immediate asks:
1) Priyom/Vivek: quick triage — can we identify whether this is algorithmic backpressure (batching + seq length) or infrastructure (node OOMs / network) within 20m?
2) Marissa: can you prepare an exec note for TideBank leadership + recommended commercial remediation (short-term credit / burst authorization)?
3) Sofia: procurement lead — we may need to provision emergency burst capacity or approve cross-tenant headroom reallocation; what’s the fastest path?

I’m proposing a 09:00 PT triage call (30m). Please ack and share short status in thread.

Thanks,
David

On 2027-08-01 08:42, David Kim wrote:
> Team —
> 
> TideBank (TB-4821) reported a production regression...

Quick summary from infra triage (10:30 check-in):
- Root cause: workload pattern produced sustained large sequence generations (avg seq len +20% above baseline) alongside bursty request arrivals. That pushed effective batching beyond configured per-pool headroom and caused KV cache eviction churn; net effect: per-token service time increased and queue depth grew. No OOMs or network packet loss observed.
- A small set of earlier model variants we shipped for this customer have slightly more memory pressure due to recent optimizer changes — exacerbates KV churn.

Immediate mitigations applied (now):
1) Throttled max_batch on TideBank's pool from 256 -> 96 (reduces latency at cost of throughput).
2) Enabled per-tenant prefix caching (reduces rebuilds).
3) Flipped 20% of inbound traffic to hosted fallback model (redwood-hosted-v2) via routing override — expecting latency to normalize in ~5–10m.

Next steps (recommendation):
- Short-term: approve burst GPU allocation (24–48h) for TideBank to restore reserved throughput SLA while we stabilize the model config. This requires procurement + capacity ops sign-off.
- Medium-term: ship a targeted optimizer rollback/patch to reduce memory pressure and update queueing heuristics. ETA: 3 business days for patch and verification in staging; 5–7 for full production rollout with canary.

I’ll keep logs and a short postmortem draft.

—Priyom

Elena —

Summary and immediate plan:
- What happened: workload surge with longer-than-expected sequence lengths caused sustained batching and KV cache churn in your reserved pool leading to elevated p95 latency and a small spike in 502s between 07:35–08:05 PT. No node OOMs detected.
- What we did (08:30–09:10): applied batch throttling, enabled prefix caching, and routed 20% of traffic to hosted fallback (redwood-hosted-v2). These changes lowered queue depth and normalized p95 latency to ~210ms.
- What we propose (next 48h): 1) Provision a 48-hour reserved burst to restore headroom and match committed throughput; 2) Ship an optimizer rollback patch to reduce memory pressure (ETA 3 business days for canary); 3) Deliver a full post-incident report including request traces and remediation timeline.

Commercial offer: we will provide a one-time credit to TideBank for the impacted window (proposal: 10% of August usage attributed to affected endpoints) and will prioritize the patch rollout. Marissa will follow-up on exact credit wording and Finance approval.

Temporary routing note: the hosted fallback will cause an estimated ~15% increase in token-cost per affected request during the routing window; we can revert as soon as the burst is provisioned and the patch is validated.

Please confirm if you approve the burst procurement and the commercial credit offer so we can proceed. If you prefer a different remediation path (larger credit vs. longer burst), we can adapt but need quick guidance to stabilize customer experience.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability
